text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 2.9% today after hitting a three-month low yesterday, as oil prices stabilized on news of diplomatic talks between Saudi Arabia and Iran aimed at de-escalating regional tensions. The stock had fallen sharply over the past few days as crude prices spiked on Middle East conflict fears, then pulled back; today's recovery mirrors that pullback in oil prices, which fell slightly as investors digested signals that the immediate supply risk may be easing.

Refineries are running at 93.4% capacity and gasoline inventories are moderate, so the refiner's margins depend heavily on the direction of crude costs. The whipsaw in MPC's price over the past week—from $475 down to $457 and back up to $471—reflects the same underlying driver: the market rapidly repricing oil up on geopolitical shock, then down again as diplomatic hopes rose, with no fundamental shift in refining economics underneath.
